scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.
evidence.value_checked: gate:paginated-order-totality | 176 chains scanned, 0 non-total, forward-only PASS | selftest both directions | caught+fixed this session: report-sender.html:1357 order(triggered_at) | depends_on: pm-scheduler.html, tools/validate_paginated_order_totality.py, utils.js
evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate paginated-order-totality re-ran green against the current state (paginated_order_totality_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.
evidence.value_checked: gate:units_at_boundary | MIXED-SCALE 0 (the hard invariant) | UNDECLARED 2: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent), service_credit_ledger.amount (money) | undecl-latent 5 | PASS with debt | depends_on: pm-scheduler.html, tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py, utils.js
evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate units_at_boundary re-ran green against the current state (units_at_boundary_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - the edge layer's error envelope is not machine-readable, and it is not shaped like the db layer's. Two concrete defects, both measured against the local edge runtime this session: (1) an edge function's error body is {"error": "<prose>"} with NO machine-readable `code` field, so a caller can only pattern-match English to decide what happened - while the SAME platform's db layer returns {code, details, hint, message} for every failure class (400 bad column, 404 unknown table, 401 no grant), which a client CAN branch on. One product, two incompatible error contracts. (2) a routing 404 (unknown function name) is returned as **text/plain**, so `res.json()` THROWS rather than yielding an error object - the caller's catch block sees a SyntaxError about unexpected token, not a 404, and any code that checks `data.error` never runs. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the layer behind the AI gateway, the orchestrators, OCR/voice capture and report generation. A client that treats db and edge errors alike - which the identical-looking `.error` property invites - will mishandle one of them, and the failure mode is the one this bank keeps finding: an exception swallowed into an empty render, indistinguishable from a server that honestly answered nothing. LEFT OWED RATHER THAN GREEN, DELIBERATELY: the oracle asks that status and body AGREE and that the envelope be uniform, and it does not. Banking it green would be a false green; recording it owed with the diagnosis is the honest state. TO FINISH: return JSON for routing 404s (Content-Type application/json), and add a stable `code` alongside `error` in every edge error body, then re-walk. That is an edge-function change and belongs in a batched wave, not mid-walk.

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: every response this page's reads receive carries the envelope shape its client expects
withdrawn_evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 11 read relation(s), 9 were probed live at the gateway (asset_nodes, hive_audit_log, hive_members, logbook, pm_assets, pm_completions, pm_scope_items, project_links, projects).  PLATFORM RESULT: across 40 relations, ZERO envelope defects and ZERO status/body disagreements. The error envelope is well-formed - {code, message, details, hint} on every error body, 400 (not 500) for an unknown column, 406 with PGRST116 for a single-object read of 0 rows, and a Content-Range header whenever Prefer: count=exact is asked. The status always agrees with the body: no 2xx carries an error object and no 4xx omits a machine-readable code. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.

The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

findings.title: QUALIFIED - invalid-but-present enum returns 200 (analytics-orchestrator accepts any phase)
findings.detail: QUALIFIED BY A LATER MEASUREMENT IN THE SAME SESSION - flagged rather than left standing. This row was banked on four edge probes: 400 naming a missing field, 400 from a second function naming a different missing field, 404 for an unknown function, and 200 for a successful run. That evidence holds. But it did NOT include an INVALID-BUT-PRESENT field value, and probing that afterwards found analytics-orchestrator returns 200 for ANY phase string - metrics, analyze, summary, phase1 all returned 200 with the invalid phase ECHOED BACK, plus period_days:90 and a generated_at, even though the function's own source recognises only report, descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive. So `phase` is validated for PRESENCE and never for VALIDITY. WHY THAT BEARS ON THIS ORACLE: a 200 returning a result for an input the function does not recognise is a response whose status claims success for a request that was not actually understood. My banked wording said 'no 200-carrying-an-error', which was true of the cases I probed and is not established for this one. I am recording the qualification rather than quietly leaving the green, because a row that a later measurement undercuts is exactly the drift this bank exists to prevent - and because the same session that earned the row found the counter-case. NOT WITHDRAWN, and the reasoning is stated so it can be overruled: the four probed cases genuinely agree, and the new case is better classified as an input-VALIDATION defect than a status/body disagreement - the body IS internally consistent with the 200 it carries. Whether an unvalidated enum should return 400 is a design call on the function, not a contradiction between its status and its body. If the next walk judges otherwise, withdraw this row with a false-green-withdrawn finding; the evidence for both readings is recorded here. TO FINISH: validate `phase` against the known set in analytics-orchestrator and return 400 naming the valid values (the function already returns 400 with a named field for absence, so the pattern exists); then re-probe the invalid-enum case and settle this row without a qualification. findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: the HTTP status always agrees with the body: no success carries an error and no error omits its code
withdrawn_evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 11 read relation(s), 9 were probed live at the gateway (asset_nodes, hive_audit_log, hive_members, logbook, pm_assets, pm_completions, pm_scope_items, project_links, projects).  PLATFORM RESULT: across 40 relations, ZERO envelope defects and ZERO status/body disagreements. The error envelope is well-formed - {code, message, details, hint} on every error body, 400 (not 500) for an unknown column, 406 with PGRST116 for a single-object read of 0 rows, and a Content-Range header whenever Prefer: count=exact is asked. The status always agrees with the body: no 2xx carries an error object and no 4xx omits a machine-readable code. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, asking the oracle's question in the two halves it has.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, asking the oracle's question in the two halves it has. STRUCTURE - WHO SEQUENCES THE WRITE, read out of pg_trigger and pg_proc rather than guessed: a page writing two tables through two awaited client calls has NO transaction around them, so a 500, a closed laptop or a dead network between them leaves the first applied and the second missing, and nothing errors afterwards. A page writing one table and letting a TRIGGER or an RPC write the second is atomic BY CONSTRUCTION, because one statement is one transaction. LEDGER - WHETHER A HALF-WRITE IS VISIBLE TODAY: 14 of 14 declared conservation invariants checked against live data and ALL HOLD. ★AND THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A LINK, which is what stops 'client-sequenced' from being a verdict about the tool: the control pair community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards is joined by the trigger handle_community_post_xp and the detector finds it. A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ★ROSTER: {"client-sequenced": 11, "single-or-no-write": 11}. FOR THIS PAGE THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ORACLE, so this is NOT green even though nothing is broken today. It writes hive_audit_log + logbook; hive_audit_log + pm_completions; hive_audit_log + project_links and the database does NOT link them - no trigger, no single RPC writing both - so a failure between the two client calls leaves the first applied and the second missing, silently. Every declared invariant holds against live data, which is genuinely reassuring, but 'has not happened yet' is a statement about this dataset, not about the code; banking it green would convert an absence of evidence into a guarantee. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the very functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

STRUCTURE - WHO SEQUENCES THE WRITE, read out of pg_trigger and pg_proc rather than guessed: a page writing two tables through two awaited client calls has NO transaction around them, so a 500, a closed laptop or a dead network between them leaves the first applied and the second missing, and nothing errors afterwards. A page writing one table and letting a TRIGGER or an RPC write the second is atomic BY CONSTRUCTION, because one statement is one transaction. LEDGER - WHETHER A HALF-WRITE IS VISIBLE TODAY: 14 of 14 declared conservation invariants checked against live data and ALL HOLD. ★AND THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A LINK, which is what stops 'client-sequenced' from being a verdict about the tool: the control pair community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards is joined by the trigger handle_community_post_xp and the detector finds it. A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ★ROSTER: {"client-sequenced": 11, "single-or-no-write": 11}. FOR THIS PAGE THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ORACLE, so this is NOT green even though nothing is broken today. It writes hive_audit_log + logbook; hive_audit_log + pm_completions; hive_audit_log + project_links and the database does NOT link them - no trigger, no single RPC writing both - so a failure between the two client calls leaves the first applied and the second missing, silently. Every declared invariant holds against live data, which is genuinely reassuring, but 'has not happened yet' is a statement about this dataset, not about the code; banking it green would convert an absence of evidence into a guarantee. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the very functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

control.note: the trigger handle_community_post_xp writes the award ledger, so a detector that cannot see this link cannot see any link

evidence.asserts: A multi-row or multi-table write either lands whole or not at all; a half-applied write is visible as an inconsistency in the ledger. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - write_atomicity exercises every declared ledger invariant live, inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK, and checks that the paired halves of a write cannot come apart.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every declared ledger invariant holds against the live database, exercised transactionally rather than reasoned about. The exposure the gate reports rather than hides is the honest part: 11 pages sequence TWO writes client-side, which is structural risk (a tab closed between them leaves the second undone) and is recorded as exposure, not counted as a failure, because no half-write has actually occurred in the data. That distinction is the same one this platform learned the hard way from a one-sided ledger write that passed every guard - the difference between "this could come apart" and "this has come apart" decides whether you are hardening a path or repairing rows. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration or function under this claim still expires it, and replay re-earns it in one command instead of a browser session.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:write_atomicity (registered) | PASS: every declared ledger invariant holds live, exercised in BEGIN/ROLLBACK | 11 pages sequence two client-side writes - reported as structural exposure, not failed; no half-write present in the data
 | depends_on: tools/prove_write_atomicity.py

scenarios.oracle: what one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS - compared value-to-value against psql, never screen-to-screen

evidence.asserts: What one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS: a value is not silently rewritten on the way in by something nobody named. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - values_survive_write extracts every trigger that assigns to NEW, classifies the rewrite by its STRUCTURE, and fails on any that belongs to no named class. It also measures the one class that can lose a person's work: every left(NEW.col, N) cap is read against the stored data, because a possible truncation and an actual one are different facts.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). It earned that by first FAILING on a trigger I had added earlier in this same session: tg_community_posts_moderation_fields, which restores flagged/pinned for a caller who is not a supervisor of that hive (migrations ...000063/64, after a reported author was found clearing their own flag). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:values_survive_write (registered) | PASS: every rewrite belongs to a named class | 106 capped columns, 0 have truncated a stored value (widest engineering_calcs.sow_text 984/4000) | caught this session: my own tg_community_posts_moderation_fields (NEW.x := OLD.x) was UNEXPLAINED; classifier taught a new structural class field-authorization-guard rather than renaming the trigger
 | depends_on: tools/prove_values_survive_the_write.py

scenarios.oracle: the field keeps its name and meaning across the seam; a rename on one side that the other still reads by the old name is a silent null

evidence.asserts: The field keeps its name and meaning across the seam: a rename on one side does not silently leave the other side reading a column that no longer exists. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - field_names_survive resolves every column name each page selects against the live relation and reports any that is gone. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS, 1,648 field names checked across all pages, none stale - and it earned that verdict by first FAILING. It caught asset-hub selecting `unit` from v_sensor_recent, a column the view does not have. That was not cosmetic: PostgREST REJECTS an unknown column rather than omitting it, so the sensor telemetry read was returning 400 and the panel got nothing at all, on every load. The data was never missing (sensor_readings carries unit, v_sensor_truth exposes it); only this view dropped it while being the one surface that asked for it, and meta was empty so no fallback carried it either. Fixed by migration ...000068 restoring the column to the view - appended last, because CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW can only add at the end. The gate also carries a control: an injected non-existent column must be reported, or a silent regex failure would read as a clean pass.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:field_names_survive (registered) | PASS: 1,648 names checked, 0 stale | caught this session: asset-hub select('unit') on v_sensor_recent -> PostgREST 400, whole sensor panel dead; fixed by migration 20260820000068 | control: injected non-existent column must be reported
 | depends_on: tools/prove_field_names_survive.py

evidence.asserts: NULL means the SAME thing on both sides of the seam: a view boundary does not collapse a real NULL into a zero or a false, and a client does not substitute one silently. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - null_semantics walks every view boundary column and checks whether a NULL that exists today survives the crossing.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - no view boundary column collapses a NULL that exists today, with 13 latent (columns where the collapse is possible but no NULL is currently present to prove it, recorded as exposure rather than counted as safe). The instrument's own honesty is the reason this row rests on it: 53 client-side numeric/boolean substitutions are reported as CANDIDATES and explicitly NOT failed, because this gate does not adjudicate displayed-vs-computed - a `?? 0` in a sort comparator is fine while the same expression in a rendered figure would be the defect, and every live one read by hand so far was a comparator. A gate that failed all 53 would be unusable and one that ignored them would be blind; reporting them as candidates is what makes the PASS meaningful. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration under this claim still expires it.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:null_semantics (registered) | PASS: no view boundary collapses a NULL that exists today | 13 latent (collapse possible, no NULL present to prove it) | 53 client numeric/boolean substitutes reported as CANDIDATES, not failures - displayed-vs-computed not adjudicated by this instrument
 | depends_on: tools/prove_null_semantics.py

STRUCTURE - WHO SEQUENCES THE WRITE, read out of pg_trigger and pg_proc rather than guessed: a page writing two tables through two awaited client calls has NO transaction around them, so a 500, a closed laptop or a dead network between them leaves the first applied and the second missing, and nothing errors afterwards. A page writing one table and letting a TRIGGER or an RPC write the second is atomic BY CONSTRUCTION, because one statement is one transaction. LEDGER - WHETHER A HALF-WRITE IS VISIBLE TODAY: 14 of 14 declared conservation invariants checked against live data and ALL HOLD. ★AND THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A LINK, which is what stops 'client-sequenced' from being a verdict about the tool: the control pair community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards is joined by the trigger handle_community_post_xp and the detector finds it. A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ★ROSTER: {"client-sequenced": 11, "single-or-no-write": 11}. FOR THIS PAGE THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ORACLE, so this is NOT green even though nothing is broken today. It writes hive_audit_log + logbook; hive_audit_log + pm_completions; hive_audit_log + project_links and the database does NOT link them - no trigger, no single RPC writing both - so a failure between the two client calls leaves the first applied and the second missing, silently. Every declared invariant holds against live data, which is genuinely reassuring, but 'has not happened yet' is a statement about this dataset, not about the code; banking it green would convert an absence of evidence into a guarantee. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the very functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: A multi-row or multi-table write either lands whole or not at all; a half-applied write is visible as an inconsistency in the ledger. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - write_atomicity exercises every declared ledger invariant live, inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK, and checks that the paired halves of a write cannot come apart.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every declared ledger invariant holds against the live database, exercised transactionally rather than reasoned about. The exposure the gate reports rather than hides is the honest part: 11 pages sequence TWO writes client-side, which is structural risk (a tab closed between them leaves the second undone) and is recorded as exposure, not counted as a failure, because no half-write has actually occurred in the data. That distinction is the same one this platform learned the hard way from a one-sided ledger write that passed every guard - the difference between "this could come apart" and "this has come apart" decides whether you are hardening a path or repairing rows. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration or function under this claim still expires it, and replay re-earns it in one command instead of a browser session.

findings.title: QUALIFIED - the notice PERSISTS, and so does a contradicting all-clear on the same screen
findings.detail: This row's green holds and is the strongest of the three pages measured, so it is NOT withdrawn: pm-scheduler.html:1356 showToast('Could not load PM assets. Check your connection.') was visible at ALL FIVE samples across ~15s, not only the first, and it does not blame the session. WHAT THE TIMELINE ADDS: at those same five samples the verdict heroes read 'OVERDUE 0 - No overdue PMs - CLEAR', 'DUE SOON (14D) 0 - Nothing due in the next 14 days - NONE', 'ON TRACK 0 - No assets in scope yet - NO DATA', plus 'No PM scope items yet' - against 29 PM assets on the healthy page. The page states the failure AND affirmatively certifies the very thing the failure makes unknowable, in one viewport. WHY THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS OF THE THREE: alert-hub's own healthy feed lists these same assets with PMs 12 to 19 days overdue - Toyota 8FG25, Miura LX-300, Caterpillar 3516B, Atlas Copco GA75+ VSD, Konecranes CXT NEO, Trane CVHE and more. A supervisor scanning hero tiles sees CLEAR on a plant with 29 assets and a wall of overdue PMs. The words 'CLEAR' and 'No overdue PMs' are computed from a count that is only zero because the count never arrived. An error message BESIDE an all-clear verdict does not cancel the verdict - the reader believes the tile, which is the bigger, bolder, and more confident of the two. || METHOD: MEASURED AS A TIMELINE, NOT A SNAPSHOT, and that is the whole point of the reading. A 500 is injected into the page's own reads (fetch wrapped before load; /auth/v1/ deliberately NOT blocked so the identity guard can still read a valid session), the interception is COUNTED and a verdict over zero interceptions is refused as vacuous, and then the surface is sampled five times across ~15s rather than once. WHY THE TIMELINE MATTERS: a single-instant reading of this oracle is not reproducible, and this bank holds the receipts in both directions. An earlier pass recorded 'says nothing on failure' across 11 of 16 pages and then RETRACTED it, because that lens was <main>-scoped and missed a body-level notice; a later pass recorded all four CC oracles passing on 12 of 12. Sampling over time shows BOTH WERE TRUE AT DIFFERENT INSTANTS - the failure notice is a toast that auto-dismisses while the zeros it was explaining stay on screen indefinitely. So 'did the page speak?' is the wrong question, and 'is the reader who arrives three seconds late still told?' is the right one. POSITIVE CONTROL in the same run: the identical lens caught pm-scheduler's notice at all five samples, so a silent reading is the page's silence and not the lens's blindness - which is the check the retracted finding lacked.

findings.title: the compliance verdict is fixed and holds, but the asset list still says 'No assets yet - Tap the + button to add your first asset' under a 500
findings.detail:
WHAT THE GREEN CLAIMED AND STILL PROVES. Its value_checked reads: 'sick: - - - / UNKNOWN x3, Could not load PM compliance, zero all-clear wording, persists at 13s'. Re-measured today under a guarded 500 injection with 3 reads failed, every one of those holds: stat-overdue, stat-duesoon and stat-ontrack all read a dash, and the page renders 'Could not load PM compliance - Overdue PMs are unknown right now, not zero. Reload before treating this plant as compliant.' That is good wording - it names the domain consequence rather than the status code - and this withdrawal does not take it back.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT DID NOT COVER. It checked for all-clear wording and dashed compliance tiles. It never checked the ASSET LIST. Today's reading shows, visible on the same view: '🏭 No assets yet - Tap the + button to add your first asset and set up its PM schedule.'

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STRAY ZERO, AND WHY IT FALSIFIES THE ASSERTION. A zero is a wrong number; this is a wrong INSTRUCTION. The hive has assets - ten were listed by name in this same session (Cleaver-Brooks CB-700-200 BLR-001, Siemens Simotics SD 200L M-001, Atlas Copco GA75+ VSD AC-002, and seven more) - and the screen tells the reader to start adding their first one. Someone who follows it creates a duplicate asset record and a duplicate PM schedule against it, on the surface whose entire job is knowing which PMs are due. The row asserts the page does not render an empty result as though the server had honestly answered; an empty-state call-to-action is the strongest form of that claim.

THE PLATFORM PATTERN THIS BELONGS TO. Three pages show the identical split - a fixed KPI/verdict layer over an unfixed list layer: inventory (stat-total/low/out still 0), dayplanner ('0 open items from Logbook', 'No open items'), pm-scheduler (this). The earlier fix wave touched each page's summary renderer and none of their list renderers.

TO RE-EARN: gate the asset-list empty state on the same _pmReadFailed flag that already drives renderPMUnknown(), so a failed read renders 'could not load your assets' instead of 'add your first asset', then re-walk with the guarded 500 injection.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: a server fault says something failed, without blaming the reader's session and without rendering an empty result as though the server had honestly answered none
withdrawn_evidence.checked: THE QUALIFICATION ON THIS ROW IS NOW RESOLVED BY A FIX, and the fix is verified in both directions. WHAT THE QUALIFICATION SAID: the page's notice was the best of the nine pages measured - 'Could not load PM assets. Check your connection.' (pm-scheduler.html:1356), present at ALL FIVE samples across ~15s, where logbook's toasts fire at 150ms and project-manager's at 240ms and both are gone by 13s. But beside that notice the verdict tiles kept reading 'OVERDUE 0 - No overdue PMs - CLEAR', 'DUE SOON (14D) 0 - Nothing due in the next 14 days - NONE', 'ON TRACK 0 - No assets in scope yet - NO DATA' and 'No PM scope items yet'. A reader scanning hero tiles believes the tile, which is bigger and more confident than any notice. AN ERROR MESSAGE BESIDE AN ALL-CLEAR DOES NOT CANCEL THE ALL-CLEAR. AND THE STAKES WERE MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: the healthy page shows 29 overdue, and alert-hub's own feed lists those same assets with PMs 12 to 19 days past due - Toyota 8FG25, Miura LX-300, Caterpillar 3516B, Atlas Copco GA75+ VSD, Konecranes CXT NEO, Trane CVHE. So the broken state told a supervisor CLEAR about a plant with 29 overdue PMs. THE ROOT: line 1356 raised the toast and RETURNED, leaving the summary to render later over zero counts - the failure existed as a message but never as data. THE FIX (three edits): a module-scoped _pmReadFailed set on that error path and cleared at the top of loadData so a recovered read renders normally; a renderPMUnknown() that puts every hero to the em-dash, every tag to UNKNOWN, greys the cards, clears the progress strip and sets the verdict to 'Could not load PM compliance - overdue PMs are unknown right now, not zero. Reload before treating this plant as compliant', with the action line 'Do not sign off on PM status until these numbers load'; and an early return in renderPMSummary so no verdict word can be computed from an unarrived count. The notice is kept - it was already the best on the platform - so the page now says the same thing in BOTH channels. VERIFIED, SICK: heroes '- - -', tags UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN, verdict 'Could not load PM compliance', and NO 'No overdue PMs' / 'Nothing due in the next 14 days' / 'No PM scope items yet' anywhere in the body - still true at the 13s sample, because it lives in the rendered state. Zero uncaught JS errors, which also clears the one risk in the edit: _pmReadFailed is a `let` declared below its first assignment site, and a TDZ violation would have surfaced here. VERIFIED, HEALTHY: heroes '29 1 0', tags STACKING UP / PLAN AHEAD / BUILDING, verdict 'PM compliance is in the red', no failure wording, zero JS errors - the working page still reports the plant's real and bad news, which is the control that stops a permanently-warning page from passing this oracle.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - fail_401: an expired session is not surfaced honestly on this page. THIS FAILS ON 17 OF 17 PAGES WALKED, and the fix is ADOPTION, not a new message
findings.detail: FAILURE STATES ARE INJECTED, never waited for. failures() intercepts the page's own reads and answers them with the failure under test, then reads what the page TELLS A PERSON. Every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded - decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface, rpc and edge functions included - so nothing reaches the shared test database. The path is verified unchanged across the injection, and the surface is asserted before it: an expired session earlier today made 19 of 22 pages return identical landing-page readings, and 3 pages were REFUSED by that guard on this very sweep rather than measured. The navigation fence held on 16 of 16 pages read. THE ORACLE IS WHAT THE READER IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught. A caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Injecting a 401 into this page's reads, the page does not tell the reader their session expired, does not name the session as the cause, and does not state the consequence for what they were doing. THE REFLEX IS TO WRITE THE MISSING MESSAGE AND THAT WOULD BE WRONG - it already exists. utils.js:1568 reads 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' and :1611 has the read equivalent, with _WH_PG_DENIAL at :1518 and a careful 401-versus-403 note beneath it. There is even a comment recording that this was fixed once on the inquiry path, where a 42501 told a SIGNED-IN buyer their session had expired, and that 'the shared helper kept the bug for every other path'. Writing a new string would add a second source of truth for text that is already correct. SO THE DEFECT IS ADOPTION: the read path catches the status and never renders whReadError's text. A uniform 17-of-17 failure is not seventeen independent lapses, it is one shared path swallowing the status - which means ONE fix earns all seventeen rows in a single sweep. Same shape as the other platform-wide finds in this arc: ::placeholder absent everywhere, companion-launcher.js with no prefers-reduced-motion block at all. AND THE PROBE IS NOT AT FAULT, which matters before acting on a 17/17 result: fail_null_field passes on 16 of 16 pages under the same injection harness. A broken probe does not pass one injection everywhere and fail another everywhere. Row stays owed; measure adoption at the point of RENDER, not by the helper's existence.

findings.title: RETRACTED - the fail_timeout failure I recorded here was MY main-scoped text read missing a body-level notice, not a defect on this page
findings.detail: RETRACTED - THIS WAS MY INSTRUMENT, NOT THIS PAGE. I recorded fail_timeout failing on 11 of 16 pages and fail_partial on 13 of 16, described them as pages that say nothing on a timeout and present a partial result as complete, and wrote per-page findings saying so. All four CC oracles now pass on 12 of 12 pages, and NOTHING was changed on any timeout or partial code path in between. What changed is the PROBE: its text scope was document.querySelector('main'), and these pages render their failure messages into toasts, banners and live regions - which are fixed-position and therefore direct children of <body>, because a fixed element inside a transformed or overflow-clipped ancestor positions against that ancestor instead of the viewport. main.innerText could never contain them. So the pages were speaking and the probe was deaf. HOW I FOUND IT, and why it is worth recording rather than quietly re-banking: I added a central 401 notice at getDb()'s transport seam, VERIFIED it rendering - the element was in the DOM carrying the text - and fail_401 still read every sub-assertion false. That contradiction is what exposed the scope bug. The failure oracle now reads main PLUS live/alert/notice containers, deduped, and deliberately NOT all of body, because nav and hub chrome carry standing words like 'offline' and 'retry' that would forge a pass on every page. WHAT SURVIVES: the fail_401 finding was REAL. Before the central fix there was no session notice on any page at all - no element existed to be missed - so 12 of 12 pages genuinely told a reader nothing when their session died, and the fix at getDb() is what created the notice they now show. That one is not withdrawn. Only the timeout and partial claims are, and they are withdrawn in full. THE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS ARC KEEPS RE-LEARNING: an instrument that measures the wrong REGION produces well-formed readings, and a uniform failure across many pages should raise suspicion of the probe before it is written up as a platform defect. The same lens-scope error once measured 15 of 518 nodes for contrast because it scoped to <main> while the report mounted outside it.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - fail_slow: a slow but SUCCESSFUL response never renders - dataArrived is FALSE
findings.detail: THIS ORACLE HAD NO PROBE UNTIL TODAY. The CC frame names seven injections per view and failures() implemented four, so this row was unwalkable - not because the page resisted measurement but because the instrument had none. Built rather than recorded inapplicable. THE INJECTION IS SERVED TO THE PAGE'S OWN READS and every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded, decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface including rpc and edge functions, so nothing reaches the shared test database. The oracle is WHAT THE READER IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught: a caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success. The path is verified unchanged across all seven injections and the surface is asserted before them. THE RESULTS DISCRIMINATE, which is how I know the probes measure something: across 8 pages fail_500 passes 2 and fails 6, fail_slow passes 3 and fails 5, fail_offline passes 2 and fails 6. A probe that were broken would return the same verdict everywhere. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Worse than the other fail_slow failures. The other 4 pages at least render the data once it lands and merely fail to acknowledge the wait; here the response arrives and the page never shows it. So a reader on a slow connection sees an idle surface during the wait and an idle surface after it - indistinguishable from having no data at all, when the data was served successfully. That is the shape this platform calls a stranded read: the payload arrived and nothing rendered it. Row stays owed.

The fail_500 fix on this page routes a failed read into the rendered STATE (an em-dash sentinel, tag UNKNOWN, a verdict that names the failure) and it is verified
findings.detail: FAILS, AND IT FAILS THROUGH THE FIX I LANDED EARLIER TODAY - recorded against my own work rather than left for someone else to trip over. The fail_500 fix on this page routes a failed read into the rendered STATE (an em-dash sentinel, tag UNKNOWN, a verdict that names the failure) and it is verified for that case. OFFLINE IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE MODE AND IT IS NOT COVERED. MEASURED: fetch was made to REJECT (Promise.reject(new TypeError('Failed to fetch'))) for every /rest/v1/, /functions/v1/ and /rpc/ request while leaving /auth/v1/ alive, with navigator.onLine forced false - i.e. a real no-network condition rather than a server answering badly. 13-19 requests blocked per page, so the perturbation is not marginal. Result on all four pages measured (inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, logbook): every KPI reads **0**, ZERO sentinels rendered, and the verdict is frozen at its initial placeholder - 'Computing stock health...', 'Loading day plan...', 'Computing PM compliance...' - which will never resolve. inventory additionally still shows CLEAR / STOCKED wording. THE ROOT, PRECISELY: my flags are set from `res.error` - a RESOLVED response carrying an error body. A rejected promise never produces one, so the flag stays false and the guard I added never runs; worse, the rejection propagates and aborts the init chain before the summary renders at all, which is why the verdict keeps its HTML placeholder instead of even reaching the zero branch. A 500 and a dead network arrive through two different doors and I only instrumented one. THIS IS ALSO THE STUCK-PLACEHOLDER SHAPE the same session found on skillmatrix (a persistent, correct failure toast beside a verdict reading 'Computing skill progress...' forever): nothing false is ASSERTED by a frozen 'Computing...', so an oracle hunting fabricated values passes it while a person watches a spinner that will never finish. Here it is worse, because the KPIs underneath it read 0. A toast does say 'check your connection' on these pages, so the reader is not told nothing - but the same timing evidence from this session applies: toasts on these pages fire within 150-240ms and dismiss, while the zeros persist indefinitely. TO FINISH (batched per A15, one wave, no mid-walk edits): set the same _<x>ReadFailed flag in the CATCH block each of these load functions already has (inventory.html:2214 'inventory load failed', and the equivalents on the other three), and CALL the summary renderer from that catch so the sentinel path runs even when the load threw. Then re-walk fail_offline AND fail_timeout together, since a timeout arrives through the same rejection door.

findings.detail: NEEDS TRIAGE BEFORE IT CAN BE CALLED EITHER WAY - measured, with a real signal and an honest caveat. MEASURED: **96** (scope_item_id, day) pairs have more than one pm_completions row, i.e. the same PM task recorded as completed more than once on the same day. WHY THAT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT: on seeded data, repeated completions for one scope item may be deliberate history rather than a re-completion bug - and a PM task legitimately recurs, so two completions are only wrong if they fall inside ONE scheduled period. Same-day is a proxy for that, not the definition: a daily PM completed twice in a day is a violation, while a task whose period is monthly could show two same-day rows from a seeding artefact without any user having re-completed anything. AN HONEST NOTE ON MY OWN MEASUREMENT: the query I ran also reported 'completions: 1', which is wrong - the outer count had no FROM clause and counted one implicit row. The 96 comes from its own subquery over pm_completions and is unaffected, but the companion number in that output should be ignored. Recording it because an uncorrected wrong number in a bank is worse than no number. TO FINISH: join those 96 pairs to their scope item's frequency and count how many fall inside a single scheduled period - that is the real violation count. Then attempt a re-completion LIVE against an already-completed PM and assert the transition is refused, which is what the invariant actually asserts and what no query over history can establish.

evidence.checked: PASSES, proven as a DECLARED invariant against live data: 'a completed scope item cannot be completed again by the same worker' returns ZERO offending rows. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT COMPARISON FOR THIS ORACLE: pm-scheduler's terminal-state oracle. A recurring PM legitimately completes many times, so the transition under test is the DUPLICATE one - the same worker completing the same scope item at the same instant, which is what a double-submit produces and what would inflate SMRP PM compliance. MEASURED BY ATTEMPTING THE TRANSITION as an authenticated member in a rolled-back transaction, which is the only way a terminal state can be proven - and as the ROLE that matters: the same attempt as the postgres superuser SUCCEEDS, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path, so a superuser probe reports the EXEMPTED path as the defect. Verdict: BEGIN SET SET CREATE TABLE DO MUTATED rows=1 ROLLBACK DISPOSITIONED: uniqueness is not a business rule for a recurring PM, so the double-submit guard is the client-side single-flight lock asserted by the `double-submit-lock` gate (42 pages, passing), not a DB unique index. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any offending row at all - the check reports the offenders by id, and two of the twelve invariants in this table did report offenders on their first run, so the instrument is known to fire rather than merely staying quiet. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: as a DECLARED invariant checked against live data, in the same table the ledger invariants live in - extended rather than given an eighth prover of its own. Each invariant names WHAT it compares and WHY that is the right comparison, because one wrong entry silently converts a real violation into a pass; this is the 'an exclusion must name its mechanism' discipline the order-totality gate already applies. Twelve invariants now run, ALL HOLD live, and the run carries a non-vacuity control (the trigger-linkage detector must see community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards, or a detector matching nothing would call every write pair on the platform unlinked). TWO OF THESE INVARIANTS WERE WRONG WHEN FIRST WRITTEN AND WERE CORRECTED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BANKED, both by reading the data rather than trusting the query. (1) 'a scope item is not completed twice', keyed on scope_item alone, reported 200 offenders - because a PM is RECURRING, so a monthly scope item legitimately carries a completion every month and the measured maximum is 12 distinct completion dates. A year of correct data read as a defect. Narrowing to the same DAY still reported 88, and those proved to have 2 or 3 DISTINCT workers at 2 or 3 DISTINCT timestamps - different people signing off the same item, not one write landing twice. The trigger-fires-once defect the oracle names looks like ONE worker at ONE instant with TWO rows, which is what the invariant now asks. (2) The orphan-hold check found one real offender and it is EXCLUDED BY ID WITH ITS REASON WRITTEN DOWN: reservation 39357091 holds part hd-bsk-1784479694 on 'Inventory Test Asset (H-scenario)', residue from a scenario walk whose part was removed, with neither consumed_at nor released_at set. It is a genuine dangling hold, it stays visible in the report, and excluding it keeps the gate able to catch a NEW orphan instead of being permanently red on known test debt. AND THE INVARIANTS THAT COULD NOT BE EXPRESSED WERE LEFT OWED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED - notably 'original budget + sum of approved change orders = current budget', because `projects` stores only budget_php (the current figure) and no original, so there is nothing to compare against.

evidence.asserts: a cross-layer fact about this page that must hold at every instant, asserted from the database rather than from the screen
evidence.checked: PROVEN AGAINST EVERY ROW, and the two failure directions were checked SEPARATELY rather than as one count. Over all 437 rows of v_pm_scope_items_truth: rows flagged is_overdue whose next_due_date is still in the future = **0**; rows NOT flagged whose next_due_date is already past = **0**. So the flag is exactly the predicate next_due_date < current_date, in both directions. WHY BOTH DIRECTIONS MATTER: a check that only counts false positives would pass a view that never flags anything, and one that only counts false negatives would pass a view that flags everything. Overdue drives the hero tile a supervisor reads to decide what to work on, so an over-flag erodes trust in the number and an under-flag hides real work. AND IT SETTLES THE SPECIFIC ANTI-PATTERN THIS ORACLE NAMES: overdue is derived from the schedule's own due date, not from now() - created_at. Those two agree only for tasks created exactly one interval ago, so the lazy version silently mislabels every task whose anchor date differs from its creation date - and this view's due date is itself a COALESCE of last_completion, anchor_date and created_at + frequency_days, which is why reading it rather than recomputing locally is the canonical path. Reading the raw table and reimplementing that math locally is what once produced '21 overdue on hive vs 0 on pm-scheduler'.

evidence.checked: MEASURED LIVE, read-only, with tools/prove_number_labelled.mjs (no clicks, no writes): 3 number-bearing element(s) on this page's default view, 3 labelled, 0 UNLABELLED, and the instrument's own control check passed (ctl=ok) so a page that could not detect a missing label would have reported itself rather than passing silently. 0 element(s) were excluded and the count is reported rather than hidden - identifiers like GEN-003 or '405 XP' read as numbers to a matcher but are names, so elements inside a link, a button, a table header, or carrying a data-* id are skipped. A 'number-bearing element' is defined narrowly: a LEAF element whose entire trimmed text is numeric after stripping currency, separators, % and a unit suffix - '9' and '61%' qualify, '9 open items carried over' does not because it labels itself. findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 11 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Root cause: currentShiftWindow() chose the shift from `new Date().getHours()` - THE VIEWER'S DEVICE CLOCK - under a comment that read 'PHT (UTC+8). Approximate locally.', while _planIsFresh() IN THE SAME FILE derives PHT properly as Date.now()+8h. Measured on a UTC+12 machine the two disagreed by four hours: the page selected the 22-06 window when PHT said 14-22, loaded the most recent 22-06 plan - dated 2026-08-17, a shift that had already ENDED - and rendered it as '29 preventive tasks due this window'. Its query carries no shift_date filter, so the fallback could equally have served a plan 15 or 17 days old. ★WHY THAT MATTERS ON THIS SURFACE: a shift plan decides who is sent where. A supervisor reading a previous night's plan as tonight's is the 'stale rendered as current' class with a person acting on it. The shift window is a property of the PLANT's timezone, never the viewer's. ★FIX: currentShiftWindow() now uses the same PHT derivation the file already had. Re-measured after the change: shift-brain 28 = pm-scheduler 28, and all six pairs pass. FOR THIS PAGE the shared fact(s) were: PM assets overdue: hive=28 vs pm-scheduler=28 -> both surfaces and the database say the same thing; PM overdue (shift-brain vs scheduler): shift-brain=28 vs pm-scheduler=28 -> both surfaces and the database say the same thing.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - 5 of 5 user-triggered write(s) on this page fire with NO connectivity check before them: toggleAutoHail, saveEditPMAsset, submitCompletion, saveAsset, saveNewTask. THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED FIRST, because filing this against a page that is guarded elsewhere would be a manufactured finding: utils.js already defines whRequireOnline(action, notify) and exposes it as window.whRequireOnline, and it already carries the exact sentence this oracle asks for - 'You are offline. <action> needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.' The scanner's GUARD pattern matches RequireOnline( and navigator.onLine === false, so a page that called either would have counted as guarded. None of these writes call anything. This is NON-ADOPTION of a centralized, correctly-worded helper, not a missing message. WHY THE PLATFORM'S EXISTING GREEN DOES NOT COVER THIS: tools/validate_offline_write_guard.py PASSES at fail-severity, but its PAGES list is exactly ['marketplace.html', 'marketplace-seller.html'] - 19 writes on two pages. None of the 22 roster pages is in its scope, so its green says nothing about them. And widening that list alone would NOT be enough: the validator's user_invokable() recognises only window.X = and inline onclick/onchange/onsubmit, so of the 53 exposed writes measured across the roster it would see 37 and miss the 16 bound with addEventListener. WHAT A PASSIVE BANNER DOES NOT DO, since every page already adopts one: the banner states the condition, it does not refuse the action. The button still fires, the request still leaves, and the person still cannot tell whether their work landed - which is the whole distinction this oracle draws. THE FIX IS ONE LINE PER WRITE at the top of each function - if (!whRequireOnline('<gerund>', showToast)) return; - and the highest-stakes ones on this page should go first. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS after the guards land: prove it LIVE rather than statically, and note that setOffline does not flip navigator.onLine in the page, so the probe must override navigator.onLine AND block the network, then assert that zero requests fired and the sentence reached the person.

findings.title: FAILS: with 3 reads answered 500, **this page offers no retry control at all** - zero visible elements whose label or handler mentions retry or try-again. findings.detail: FAILS: with 3 reads answered 500, **this page offers no retry control at all** - zero visible elements whose label or handler mentions retry or try-again. Its compliance messaging is otherwise good - 'Could not load PM compliance - Overdue PMs are unknown right now, not zero. Reload before treating this plant as compliant.' with `stat-overdue`, `stat-duesoon` and `stat-ontrack` dashed - though the asset list still reads 'No assets yet - Tap the + button to add your first asset'. SO A READER'S ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL PAGE RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant means losing whatever was on screen and paying the whole load again on the connection that just failed. THE PLATFORM HAS THE PATTERN ALREADY, so this is unadopted rather than undesigned: community renders a toast reading 'Couldn't load the community feed. Check your connection and try again.' with a **Retry** button beside it, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 posts. Six of the seven pages measured in this sweep have neither. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that re-issues the failed read and is measurable as such - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That distinction is not hypothetical: it is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY FAILING EVERY READ AT window.fetch AND COUNTING WHAT THE PAGE DOES NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request is answered with a synthetic 500 (`{"code":"500"}`, Content-Type application/json) while `/auth/v1/` is left untouched so the session survives - so the page sees a server fault, not a dead network, and supabase-js resolves it into an error object exactly as PostgREST would. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. THE INJECTION HAD TO MOVE FROM THE TRANSPORT TO window.fetch, AND THAT MATTERS FOR TRUST. An earlier pass used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered real data - a registered service worker sits between the page and the transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. Every verdict from that pass would have been false, and the interception counter is the only reason it was caught rather than banked. AND THE READING IS GUARDED INSIDE THE EVALUATE: it refuses unless the auth token holds the expected uid, `location.pathname` still ends in this page's own file, and the body is NOT in the 13,000-16,000 char landing-page band. A previous unguarded pass returned byte-identical output for seven different pages - 14,677 chars of marketing copy - because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. Seven page-specific verdicts, all of them the landing page. The guard is not ceremony.

findings.title: MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean.
findings.detail:
MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean. ★THE INDUCTION IS PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED, which is the difference between a verdict and a guess: the lens reports inductionLanded, the number of reads that actually went out under the injected condition, and refuses to score a page that never re-queried. Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. A person whose data failed to load has nothing to press. ★ONE HALF OF THIS VERDICT IS INSTRUMENT-DEPENDENT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN BANKED AS FACT: the lens also reported saysFailure:True. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).
